findings.description: per-req-judgement rates AC-1..AC-5, AC-7, AC-8 of SEC-PROXY-005 'automatable' (ac_verifiability 10) and flags only AC-6. AC-3 ('For a target given by host name (for example https://localhost:<port>), the SNI server name the https backend receives in the TLS ClientHello is that target host name') fails as written on the JVM test runtime with the mechanism the statement mandates: SunJSSE does not put a single-label host into SNI. Probe on OpenJDK 17.0.20.1: SSLSocketFactory.getDefault().createSocket(plainConnectedSocket, "localhost", port, true).getSSLParameters().getServerNames() = null, while host "example.test" gives [type=host_name (0), value=example.test]. So the statement's 'so that SNI carries the target host name' is false for localhost and the AC's own example cannot pass without extra work.
findings.suggested_action: Amend SEC-PROXY-005 AC-3 via MCP: use a dotted target host name in the test (resolved through a package-private resolver seam) or require the client to set SNIHostName explicitly (reflective SSLParameters.setServerNames, API 24+) and drop the localhost example; re-score SEC-PROXY-005 ac_verifiability.
